architecture.physical_store_candidate: SQLite on accepted single-VPS target only when storage safety gate passes

lineage.rule: exactly one ADMITTED_CURRENT semantic lineage head
lineage.sibling_policy: same-source/same-epoch divergent siblings are distinct candidates; only one may be admitted current
lineage.recovery: restored snapshots must prove ancestry to the admitted/recovery-selected lineage and satisfy external monotonic floor

execution_binding.rule: every authoritative semantic transaction/state-epoch mutation binds immutable execution_id + lease_epoch + session/client provenance + lineage head
execution_binding.effect_fence_dependency: reuse current PASS effect execution-generation mechanism; do not duplicate provider lifecycle code
execution_binding.stale_policy: stale generation cannot commit state even if process resumes

external_floor.rule: DB generation below verified external floor => fail closed / recovery required
external_floor.warning: a copy of the floor inside the same UnifiedDB file is evidence only, not rollback protection

storage_safety_gate.wal_mode: allowed only when exact SQLite build is proven fixed/backported or machine-checked connection/checkpoint topology excludes upstream WAL-reset trigger conditions
storage_safety_gate.target_observation: current workspace reports SQLite 3.45.1 + WAL on accepted target
storage_safety_gate.upstream_fix: SQLite >=3.51.3, or named fixed backports such as 3.44.6/3.50.7; exact distribution backport still requires verification

architecture.rollback: disable enforcement + restore prior schema/application path + preserve evidence; never delete lineage/receipt history

hypothesis: A logically unified canonical state plane with physically isolated external rollback floor and derived/index sidecars gives the best current correctness/recovery tradeoff.
counterhypothesis: Keeping more state physically specialized may reduce common-mode failure and be simpler; physical consolidation should be rejected unless target measurements show material IPC/serialization savings without recovery regression.
